LanguageData.TheMoat_EdgeRoughnessDesc: How irregular the foot of the mountain is. At 0% it is a straight cliff line; higher values add bays and spurs, up to about 15% of the map deep. The mountain stays solid either way.
LanguageData.TheMoat_AllowOresDesc: If enabled, mineable ore lumps (steel, components, gold, etc.) can spawn inside the mountain. If disabled, the mountain is 100% solid natural rock.
LanguageData.TheMoat_CavesDesc: If enabled, natural tunnels like vanilla caves are dug in the inner mountain. At least {0} cells of solid rock separate them from the plains and {1} from the map edges, so a cave never opens a second way into your base. No insect hives spawn in them.
LanguageData.TheMoat_RemoveWater: Remove lakes and water on the plains
LanguageData.TheMoat_RemoveWaterDesc: If enabled, any lakes, ponds, or rivers on the plains are converted into dry soil based on local fertility.
LanguageData.TheMoat_FlattenHillsDesc: If enabled, elevation on the plains is kept flat so no rock walls or hill slopes generate on the open side.
LanguageData.TheMoat_MoatTypeDesc: A band of water on the plains along the whole foot of the mountain, also around spurs and into bays. Anyone walking to the rock face has to cross it. Shallow water freezes over in cold weather, like any shallow water; deep water never does.
LanguageData.TheMoat_MoatWidthDesc: How far the water reaches out from the foot of the mountain. A deep moat keeps a one-cell shallow bank on the plains side.
LanguageData.TheMoat_LandBridge: Land bridge in the middle: {0} cells wide
LanguageData.TheMoat_LandBridgeDesc: A strip of dry land across the moat at the middle of the mountain: a natural choke point. 0 = no land bridge.
LanguageData.TheMoat_ShallowFordsDesc: Places where the deep moat is only shallow water, {0} cells wide, at random spots along the mountain (always the same for the same tile). With 0 fords and no land bridge the moat can only be crossed by building over it or by flying.
LanguageData.TheMoat_MapShapeDesc: Mountain on one side: a solid mountain fills one side of the map and open plains the rest. Island: an island in the middle of the map, ringed by deep water, with a single way in.
LanguageData.TheMoat_IslandSize: Island size: {0} of the map width
LanguageData.TheMoat_IslandSizeDesc: How wide the island is across its middle. A band of open plains always stays between its water and the map edges.
LanguageData.TheMoat_ShoreRoughnessDesc: How irregular the island's shore is. At 0% the island is round; higher values add bays and headlands. The water follows the shore all the way round.
LanguageData.TheMoat_IslandTerrainDesc: All mountain: one solid mountain with thick roof to dig your base into; the colony starts on the plains in front of the way in. Open land: normal terrain with soil, trees and wildlife; the colony starts in the middle of the island.
LanguageData.TheMoat_IslandWater: Deep water around the island: {0} cells wide
LanguageData.TheMoat_IslandWaterDesc: Deep water all the way round the island: nobody can wade through it and it never freezes. Its outer edge is a one-cell shallow bank.
LanguageData.TheMoat_IslandPassageDesc: A straight strip of dry land across the water on the chosen side: the only way onto the island on foot. 0 = no way in; cross by building over the water or by flying.
